the_thing_worth_reading_twice: A CONDITION THAT NOTHING EVALUATES NEVER COMES TRUE, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY — the entry looks identical to one that is merely not met yet. That is worse than a missing condition, because a missing one is caught the moment somebody asks 'what opens this?'. Ask of every waiting thing: WHICH LINE OF CODE DECIDES IT. If the answer is a sentence, it is not waiting, it is stopped. The second half generalises too and is the part that nearly got shipped wrong: a machine-checkable condition is not automatically the RIGHT condition. The way to tell is to construct the cheapest world in which it is satisfied and ask whether the goal is actually met there. Here that world was two readings of zero yen, and in it the goal reports achieved with nothing achieved. Recorded as state/constraints.json a_stated_unlock_was_never_evaluated.
